Ora2Pg - Oracle to PostgreSQL database schema converter
Ora2Pg is a free tool used to migrate an Oracle database to a PostgreSQL
compatible schema. It connects to your Oracle database, scans it
automatically and extracts its structure or data, then generates SQL
scripts that you can load into your PostgreSQL database.
Ora2Pg can be used for anything from reverse engineering an Oracle
database to huge enterprise database migration or simply replicating
some Oracle data into a PostgreSQL database. It is really easy to use
and doesn't require any Oracle database knowledge other than providing
the parameters needed to connect to the Oracle database.
Ora2Pg consists of a Perl script (ora2pg) and a Perl module (Ora2Pg.pm).
The only thing you have to modify is the configuration file ora2pg.conf
by setting the DSN to the Oracle database and optionally the name of a
schema. Once that's done, you just have to set the type of export you
want: TABLE with constraints, VIEW, MVIEW, TABLESPACE, SEQUENCE,
INDEXES, TRIGGER, GRANT, FUNCTION, PROCEDURE, PACKAGE, PARTITION, TYPE,
INSERT or COPY, FDW, QUERY, KETTLE, SYNONYM.
By default, Ora2Pg exports to a file that you can load into PostgreSQL
with the psql client, but you can also import directly into a PostgreSQL
database by setting its DSN into the configuration file. With all
configuration options of ora2pg.conf, you have full control of what
- Export full database schema (tables, views, sequences, indexes), with
unique, primary, foreign key and check constraints.
- Export grants/privileges for users and groups.
- Export range/list partitions and sub partitions.
- Export a table selection (by specifying the table names).
- Export Oracle schema to a PostgreSQL 8.4+ schema.
- Export predefined functions, triggers, procedures, packages and
- Export full data or following a WHERE clause.
- Full support of Oracle BLOB object as PG BYTEA.
- Export Oracle views as PG tables.
- Provide some basic automatic conversion of PLSQL code to PLPGSQL.
- Export Oracle tables as foreign data wrapper tables.
- Show a report of an Oracle database content.
- Migration cost assessment of an Oracle database.
- Migration difficulty level assessment of an Oracle database.
- Migration cost assessment of PL/SQL code from a file.
- Migration cost assessment of Oracle SQL queries stored in a file.
- Generate XML ktr files to be used with Pentaho Data Integrator (Kettle)
- Export Oracle locator and spatial geometries into PostGIS.
- Export DIRECTORY as external table or directory for external_file extension.
- Dispatch a list of SQL orders over multiple PostgreSQL connections
- Perform a diff between Oracle and PostgreSQL database for test purposes.
- MySQL/MariaDB and Microsoft SQL Server migration.

PostgreSQL provides an extension framework for adding more functionality to PostgreSQL without having to fork the codebase. This makes it easier to bundle and distribute software across many unique PostgreSQL databases.

- Ensures reliable execution of workflows, even in the face of failures

An isometric drawing of Chronos DB: the database as a stack of slabs, an hour of history above it as glass slices, and twelve worlds beside it, each forked from the database. One world has merged. Another is held for a person, because it deletes 657 rows and the rule says 0.

|**World**|A branch of the whole database: every table, copy-on-write. Forking one copies a pointer, not the data, so it takes about 2 µs at any size. A world stores only the rows it changes. "Branch" and "world" mean the same thing.|
|**`main`**|The world that holds the real state. Every other world is forked from it, directly or from another world.|
|**Diff**|The rows a world changed since its fork, each with its before and after values. Also available as SQL statements.|
|**Merge**|Applying a world's changes to its parent. It is three-way: if both sides changed the same row, nothing is merged and the conflicts come back as rows for you to settle.|
|**Agent**|An account with its own token and a list of what it may do (`read`, `fork`, `write_own`, `merge_own`, ...), plus quotas and limits.|
|**Merge policy**|Rules an agent's merges must keep to go through without a person: `max_rows`, `max_deletes`, `review_tables`, `review_columns`, rows per hour, and more.|
|**Merge check**|A SQL query a merge's result must return no rows for, such as "every lead list still has a lead". It runs inside every merge.|
|**Review**|A merge that broke a rule waits in `SHOW REVIEWS` with its reasons. A person merges it (approve) or drops it (reject).|
|**Attach**|Running beside an existing Postgres: merges into `main` are written back to it in one checked transaction.|

A world leaves main at a fork, then works, diffs and reaches a merge. Inside the rules the merge lands on main, in an attached folder writing Postgres first. Outside them it waits for a person in SHOW REVIEWS. An undo can put the rows back within the history window.
More on each step: Concepts, Worlds reference, Merge policies guide, Merge checks guide.
|Write real data without a person reading every change|Read-only agents, or hand-built staging tables and approvals|A merge policy: changes within the rules land, the rest wait in `SHOW REVIEWS`|
|Show what they changed|Audit tables you build yourself|`diff world w`: every changed row, before and after|
|Keep the good work and drop the rest|Hand-written migrations|Merge all of a world, some tables (`only tables`), some rows (`only keys`), or `drop world`|
|Undo a bad run|Restore a backup and lose everyone's work|`UNDO AGENT bot SINCE '-2 hours'`, row by row, leaving others' changes|
|Try many things at once|Copy the database, or share one and fight over locks|Thousands of isolated worlds; 100,000 tested|
|Not act on stale data|Hope|A world can record what it read; its merge is held if that changed|
|Search while they work|A separate vector store that can't see uncommitted edits|Filters, full text and vectors (pgvector syntax) inside every world|
|Stay inside their lane|Database roles|Per-agent capabilities, quotas, time and memory limits, masked columns, one tenant's rows only|

Other things in the box: time travel (`select * from orders as of '-1 hour'`, `restore world`), simulations (`SIMULATE` many worlds and keep the best), a Postgres-compatible SQL surface with PL/pgSQL, JSONB and full text, and a write-ahead log with `fsync` on `main` and merges. Known gaps include: no C extensions or functions in languages other than SQL and PL/pgSQL (common extensions such as `vector`, `pgcrypto`, `citext`, `hstore` and `pg_trgm` are built in); `SERIALIZABLE` is refused rather than weakened; no replication or `pg_hba.conf`; text sorts by bytes unless a column has an ICU collation. Full list and tested drivers and ORMs: Postgres compatibility.
**Operations.** One process per database folder (share it through `chronos serve`). No hot standby or automatic failover. macOS 13+ and Linux only. See Operations.
